scope: Final read-only architecture review of section 109 initialization, authorization, concurrency and cleanup lifecycle design.

checks.evidence: 109.1/109.2: bootstrap lock then catalog lock; full replay, identity checks, file Sync and parent Sync stay under the catalog lock; release catalog then bootstrap before taking any case lock. Ordinary case operations never acquire bootstrap. No specified lock-order cycle.

CREATE_NEW and first provisioning frame form one bootstrap sequence. File and parent durability precede case-lock/member creation. Missing catalog with residual case directories or case locks is rejected; permanent bootstrap lock alone is not a case artifact. Empty/partial existing catalog is not silently initialized.

Startup re-Sync is required before case authorization. Recoverers converge on the same stable lock identity and recheck catalog state. Exact initial members may become ready once; incomplete or invalid members become quarantined. No lesson Start, Planner or Registry execution occurs in provisioning recovery.

109.3 limits each private fixture to one target Start; different lesson operations use different cases. Same-case contention validates ready snapshots before the race and rechecks under the case lock, with one winner and zero loser effects. Proven terminal failure permits only a fresh isolated fixture; unknown outcomes do not authorize another Start.

checks.contract: Stable external lock and cleanup resume
checks.evidence: Persistent verified case lock is outside the removable directory and is not replaced while contenders exist. Cleanup-only supervisor resume removes fixed members without opening SQLite/sidecar/key. Missing members are recoverable; anomalies remain isolated. Parent Sync precedes deleted tombstone, including the already-absent-directory fault oracle.

Complete valid frames define recovered state, not HTTP delivery. CRC is explicitly not authentication. Fixed catalog fields exclude user/lesson identifiers, credentials and arbitrary errors. Partial chains and uncertain current-process writes fail closed.

prior_findings: CAT-01, CAT-02, CAT-R3-01 and CAT-R3-02 remain closed. No new architecture blocker in this reviewed revision.
limitations: Design approval only; catalog/supervisor implementation is not established by this review.
Named-barrier concurrency, interrupted writes, recovery Sync failures, platform ACL/identity/parent-directory durability and process-death lock release remain mandatory implementation acceptance.
No tests, builds, services or source/design modifications were performed. No real classroom/model/audio acceptance claim.
